tag: the deterministic floor's run is recorded as a compression
old: if not served_by or served_by in _NOT_A_COMPRESSOR:
why: THE RISK THIS ITEM MUST NOT REALISE. A string always comes back — the floor composes structured output for any prompt — so treating a returned string as a compression is exactly the defect the brief's hard-coded compress_noise_to_meaning committed. The state turns on WHO SERVED the call, not on whether text arrived.

tag: an uncompressed record gets its fields filled in anyway
why: The empty values LOOK harmless and each one is a finding: an empty escalations list says there is nothing to escalate, and an empty missing list says nothing is absent — about a request nobody read. The bar's words are 'no field is filled by inference', and a default is an inference.

tag: a model that answered partially has the rest filled in for it
new: rec.update({k: _f.get(k, "" if k not in ("missing", "escalations") else []) for k in _COMPRESSION_FIELDS})
why: The subtler half of the same rule: a real compression that omitted two lines must leave them ABSENT, not defaulted. The prompt explicitly tells the model to omit what it cannot determine, so filling those in would overwrite a deliberate refusal with a claim.

tag: a term with no instrument reports that it passed
old: _has_esc = bool(_esc) if isinstance(_esc, list) else None
new: _has_esc = bool(_esc) if isinstance(_esc, list) else False
why: False says the compression looked for escalations and found none; None says there was no compression to look. Collapsing the two makes an unavailable term indistinguishable from a satisfied one, which is how a decision comes to rest on checks that never ran.

tag: an uncompressed request with an unknown domain proceeds
why: On this deployment nothing compresses, so the domain is usually ABSENT — and an absent domain cannot be shown to be outside the grave set. Requiring a KNOWN grave domain makes the fail-closed rule unreachable on the only path that actually runs, so every uncompressed request would proceed.

tag: NOT ASSESSABLE becomes a quiet PROCEED
why: A decision over a record that could not be read is a decision about nothing. This is the same shape as a gate that clears on a missing field, which P3.14 removed from the clearance chain and W543 from the homeostasis shim.

tag: an engine may write the user's own words
why: The Owner's ruling: the reflection tag holds the USER'S OWN WORDS. An AI-written value here is the platform's account of the person replacing the person's own — the one outcome this field exists to prevent, and the sharpest case of the item's no-field-is-filled-by-inference leg.

tag: a cleared tag keeps the name of whoever set it
old: r["reflection_tag_by"] = _by if _text is not None else None
why: Clearing is the user's to do and must leave no trace of what was said or that they said it. A cleared tag still naming its author records that the user wrote something and withdrew it, which is a fact about them they chose to remove.

tag: the refusal stops saying it is the ordinary path
old: f"IS THE ORDINARY PATH on this deployment, not an edge case — no model is "
new: f"is a fallback on this deployment — no model is "
why: The bar states it explicitly: the floor's run produces NOT_COMPRESSED with a reason, and IT IS THE COMMON PATH, NOT AN EDGE CASE. A refusal presented as a fallback invites a reader to treat the compressed case as normal and this one as a fault to engineer away. The first attempt at this blind used a TWO-LINE anchor that matched nothing and the harness reported BAD BLIND rather than VACUOUS — the distinction W503 built, and the reason a zero-match is not quietly read as a guard that cannot fail.
